title: Creation, Annihilation, Fission and Fusion
notes: **Particle creation:** high-energy photons can create particle-antiparticle pairs: $\gamma \rightarrow e^+ + e^-$. Energy is converted to mass.
**Annihilation:** matter-antimatter pairs can annihilate into pure energy: $e^+ + e^- \rightarrow \gamma + \gamma$. Mass is converted back to energy.
**Nuclear fission:** a heavy nucleus splits into lighter fragments, releasing energy. Example: $^{235}_{92}\text{U} + n \rightarrow ^{141}_{56}\text{Ba} + ^{92}_{36}\text{Kr} + 3n + \text{energy}$.
**Chain reaction:** neutrons from one fission can trigger further fissions. Critical mass is the minimum amount needed to sustain a chain reaction.
**Nuclear fusion:** light nuclei combine to form heavier nuclei, releasing energy. Example: $^2_1\text{H} + ^3_1\text{H} \rightarrow ^4_2\text{He} + n + 17.6\,\text{MeV}$. Powers the Sun.
